structure: North Dakota Social Studies Content Standards (Rev7, 11/30/2023; cover dated August 2019). Front matter (credits, foreword, revision log, TOC, introduction, references). Standards are written in grade bands, not single grades; districts set grade-level benchmarks. Grades K-5 section: four strands (Civics & Government, Economics, Geography, History), each first printed as a list of standards by band (codes C.K_2.1 = strand.band.number, C.3_5.1; diamond marks Century Code items), then repeated in tables per theme with columns 'Grades K-2' | 'Grades 3-5' | 'Guiding Questions' (guiding questions column is shared by both bands; treated as examples). Grades 6-12 section: eight strands/courses (Civics & Government, Economics, Geography, United States History, World History, North Dakota Studies, Sociology, Psychology), each with intro narrative then a table 'Code | Standard | Benchmarks | Guiding Topics' (C.6_12.2 = standard, C.6_12.2.1 = benchmark). US History (5 eras, codes US.6_12.1-6.E1.1), World History (4 eras, WH.6_12.1-6.E1.1), Sociology (4 domains, SOC.6_12.1-2.D1.1) and Psychology (8 domains, PSY.6_12.1-3.D1.1) repeat the same anchor standards under each era/domain with era/domain-specific benchmarks; Guiding Topics are the examples column. Extraction wraps the underscore of the printed code (C.6_12 shown as 'C.6 12') and puts a trailing ' _' on wrapped lines. Appendix A: scope and sequence (K-5 optional progression chart per grade K-5 with topic cells per grade column, plus K-12 Options A/B). Appendix B: Native American Essential Understandings (NDNAEU 1-7) and two Inquiry Design Model blueprints. Appendix C: civics learning design. Appendix D: ND literacy standards (RH, WHST) for grades 6-12. In the 6-12 section each strand is labeled as a course (course = strand title as written) with grades 6-12.

issues: Judgment call: the 6-12 strands are not formally courses in the document (standards 'do not specify a course'), but each strand has its own standards/benchmarks, and Appendix A names Economics, Government, Geography, World History, US History and elective courses. I set course to the strand title (Civics & Government, Economics, Geography, United States History, World History, North Dakota Studies, Sociology, Psychology) with grades 6-12 for units u359-u1005. K-5 strands have course null.
u195-u210: page 10 'How to read' sample table repeats Civics standard C.K_2.5/C.3_5.5 text; labeled backup (illustration, duplicate of u230-u231).
u315-u356: pages 19-20 coding-example tables repeat C.6_12.2.1-2 and US.6_12.1 Era 1 standards; labeled backup as coding examples (full versions at u382-u387 and u587-u605).

K-5 standards appear twice: as a plain list (u214-u216, u236-u238, u257-u259, u284-u285) and again in the theme tables; both labeled standards, grades by band. Extraction of the table cells has ' _' line-wrap artifacts.
K-5 'Guiding Questions' cells span both bands: grades K-5 where both K-2 and 3-5 cells exist; u253 and u281 set to 3-5 because the K-2 cell for that theme is empty.
u251, u279: 'Guiding Questions' header cells labeled K-5 examples even though the National Economy and Human Population themes have no K-2 standards.
u284: one unit merges the heading 'K-5 History Standards' with the K-2 list; labeled K-2 standards.

u1019-u1035: Appendix A page 47 graphic (My Family/School/Community/State/Country/World) was extracted as table cells with merged columns; grades assigned by column start (u1028-u1029 K, u1030 1-2, u1031-u1032 3, u1033-u1034 4, u1035 5), uncertain. Treated as examples.

u1038-u1274: Appendix A K-5 progression chart. Grade columns: C1=K, C2=1, C3=2, C5=3, C6=4, C7=5 (C4 empty). Topic cells labeled examples with their single grade; repeated standard statements and their wrapped continuation lines (K-2 in C1, 3-5 in C5) labeled backup. A topic cell cannot be separated from its continuation lines with certainty in a few rows (e.g. u1048-u1049, u1104-u1105, u1231, u1254-u1255).
